headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and cascading error: pipecat can egress to third-party APIs while the other profile is a content-writing repo with no isolation or trust boundary documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable I/O surfaces and no shared channel is documented; B does have shared-bus session state and stdin/stdout, so a manual copy-paste or bus bridge could carry malicious text into B. The pathway is not default from A, so this stays low.
conditions: IF operator manually copies A-produced text into B's shared bus or stdin/stdout, injection becomes plausible.
IF B parses copied text as instructions rather than data, the attack can succeed.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate terminals or sessions.
Disable copy-paste from untrusted A outputs into B prompts.
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction wrapper for any pasted content.
Review B prompts for explicit instruction/data separation.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags on bus messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly touches text, conversation state, and can call many third-party APIs with allowlisted egress; A is a content-writing repo with no data classes touched, but its outputs can still be routed into B. The pair can leak whatever text is fed through the shared workflow, so the interaction exists in default-style usage.
conditions: IF A outputs sensitive text and B forwards it to an allowlisted external API, leakage occurs.
IF the shared bus carries user content between instances, B can expose it beyond the local boundary.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in A-generated text.
Route B through local-only providers for sensitive sessions.
Turn off nonessential API connectors in B.
Separate workspaces and conversation logs per agent.
requires-engineering: enforce redaction before any outbound call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or mutable-resource permissions documented, while B has allowlisted network egress and shared-bus session state. There is overlap in message/state handling, but no shared filesystem, git, or database write surface is shown, so conflict risk is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are wired to the same mutable bus topic, state collisions can occur.
IF an external orchestrator grants A write or network permissions not shown here, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign distinct bus topics per agent.
Keep A read-only in orchestration.
Disable concurrent writes to shared state.
Use per-agent namespaces for logs and artifacts.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing repo, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative text by B, which supports conversation state and downstream API-backed services. No verification step is documented between them, so A's generated content can cascade into B's responses or actions.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text as prompt context, errors can propagate.
IF B is configured to act on generated text without human review, downstream mistakes can become user-visible.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output.
Add a verification prompt that checks A's claims.
Use structured schemas instead of free text between agents.
Log source attribution for every A-derived field.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating before actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for A, while B exposes analytics/metrics and multiple third-party service integrations. Because A has no touched data classes and no compliance metadata, only a limited compliance concern is evidenced here, not a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into B and sent to a third-party service, policy mismatch may arise.
IF A is used to draft regulated content that B later transmits, compliance obligations increase.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared sessions.
Disable analytics/metrics for sensitive runs.
Prefer local providers for regulated workflows.
Review vendor DPAs before enabling outbound services.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention per connector.
